findings.claim: “Hardy uses regular four-line stanzas with a refrain”
findings.truth: 'Midnight on the Great Western' is four stanzas of five lines each.
findings.evidence: data/canonical_poems/ocr-youth-and-age/midnight-on-the-great-western.txt

findings.claim: “The poem ends with the child’s imagination expanding outward: ‘These yellow flowers / Go on forever. / Almost to Detroit. / Almost to the sea.’”
findings.truth: Those lines sit before the mother's words. The poem ends: 'My playhouse is underneath / Our house, & I hear people / Telling each other secrets.'
findings.evidence: data/canonical_poems/ocr-youth-and-age/venus-s-flytraps.txt, final five lines

findings.claim: “Sheers’s poem is narrated by a parent climbing a mountain with their ageing father”, and later “The child has become the stronger one; the parent is ageing”
findings.truth: The speaker is the son. The lesson's own next paragraph says so ('The son has grown'), so the lesson contradicts itself.
findings.evidence: data/canonical_poems/ocr-youth-and-age/farther.txt: 'your bent head the colour of the rocks'

findings.claim: “For 40-mark comparison questions, your second poem should genuinely extend or challenge the argument of your first”
findings.truth: There is no 40-mark comparison. The poetry question is worth 40 marks in total but is split into two 20-mark parts, and the comparison in part (a) is against an unseen poem, not a second cluster poem.
findings.evidence: specs/ocr/english-literature-J352.md, component 02: 40 marks for the poetry section, one question in two parts (a) named anthology poem with an unseen poem, (b) a different anthology poem of own choice

findings.claim: Two questions labelled “40 marks — Poetry Comparison” asking students to compare two collection poems; four labelled “20 marks — Extract Comparison”
findings.truth: Each part of the poetry question is 20 marks. Nothing in this section uses an extract, and the four single-poem tasks are part (b) style responses.
findings.evidence: specs/ocr/english-literature-J352.md, component 02

findings.claim: Match option: “Refrain repeating the boy’s name to suggest perpetual transition”
findings.truth: Hardy never names the boy. The refrain is the description 'the journeying boy'. The lesson body says the same thing, so the answer key contradicts the teaching.
findings.evidence: data/canonical_poems/ocr-youth-and-age/midnight-on-the-great-western.txt

findings.claim: “The examiners reward four things: … a personal, critical response; analysis of language, form and structure; awareness of context; and … sustained comparative writing. These are the four assessment objectives”
findings.truth: Comparison is not an assessment objective. The fourth one is vocabulary, sentence structure, spelling and punctuation, and it is assessed only on the Shakespeare section, never on the poetry question.
findings.evidence: specs/ocr/english-literature-J352.md, AO table and 'Assessment of extended responses': the fourth objective is assessed in section B of each component only

findings.claim: “The invented word ‘Bewrapt’ (wrapped in a stupor)”
findings.truth: 'Bewrapt' is an archaic past participle of 'bewrap', not a Hardy coinage. The lesson's own flashcard calls it 'archaic', so the lesson contradicts itself.
findings.evidence: Oxford English Dictionary, 'bewrap' v., attested from Middle English; flashcard 7 in this lesson

findings.claim: “The apostrophe-like ending collapses the specific event into myth”, with a pop-up defining apostrophe as “a rhetorical question posed to an absent person”
findings.truth: The closing couplet addresses nobody, so it is not apostrophe. The pop-up definition is also wrong and contradicts this lesson's own glossary entry for apostrophe.
findings.evidence: data/canonical_poems/ocr-youth-and-age/cold-knap-lake.txt, final couplet; glossary_terms in this lesson

findings.claim: “In the exam you will not have the texts in front of you”
findings.truth: The paper is closed text, but the named anthology poem for part (a) is printed alongside the unseen poem. Only the part (b) poem must be recalled from memory.
findings.evidence: specs/ocr/english-literature-J352.md, component 02: part (a) is a comparison of a named poem from the anthology with an unseen poem

findings.claim: “the child’s wet dress, the mother’s heroism, the father’s violent punishment”
findings.truth: The speaker's father takes the rescued child home and watches her thrashed there; he is not the one who punishes her. The soaked frock in the poem belongs to the mother.
findings.evidence: data/canonical_poems/ocr-youth-and-age/cold-knap-lake.txt: 'my father took her home to a poor house / and watched her thrashed for almost drowning'; 'her wartime cotton frock soaked'

findings.claim: Heading “Quotation Bank: Eight Key Quotations”
findings.truth: Only four quotations are present. The second block was dropped during authoring. Retitled to four; authoring four more is a content job, not a fact-check fix.
findings.evidence: raw/L08.txt, content_html

findings.evidence: raw/L08.txt, content_html

findings.claim: “what two-word phrase describes the moment of death?” for 'Little — less — nothing!'
findings.truth: The phrase is three words.
findings.evidence: data/canonical_poems/ocr-youth-and-age/out-out.txt

findings.claim: Mark-scheme band names vary across the unit: 'Top band / Upper-mid band / Lower-mid band / Lower band' in lessons 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7, and 'Mastering / Secure / Developing / Emerging' in lessons 2 and 8
findings.truth: Neither ladder matches the house ladder (Top band / Upper-mid band / Mid band / Lower-mid band / Low band / Basic band). This belongs to the band-ladder relabelling queue, not to this fact-check.
findings.evidence: scripts/_retrofc/CHECK_PROMPT.md, banned strings and house ladder

findings.claim: The Frost poem is written as 'Out-Out' throughout
findings.truth: The title is “‘Out, Out—’”, quoting Macbeth. Not edited: it recurs in the body, the practice questions, the knowledge checks and the flashcards, so it is a one-pass relabel job.
findings.evidence: data/canonical_poems/ocr-youth-and-age/out-out.txt header

summary: Six of the eight lessons (1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7) are built on poems that are not in the OCR Youth and Age cluster and need rebuilding rather than editing. Lessons 2 and 8 are fully on-cluster and are fixed here: 18 edits covering the invented 40-mark and 30-mark totals, the false fourth assessment objective, a wrong speaker in 'Farther', a wrong ending for 'Venus's-flytraps', wrong stanza length in Hardy, and a misread of who punishes the child in 'Cold Knap Lake'.
